answer:
The simulation models spray combustion of liquid n-dodecane injected into hot co-flow air in a cylindrical chamber, solved with OpenFOAM's reactingParcelFoam solver in a 2D axisymmetric half-domain.
The domain is 0.2 m in the axial (x) direction by 0.05 m in the radial (r) direction, representing a cylinder 0.2 m long and 0.1 m in diameter.
The mesh is 100 cells in x by 50 cells in r, generated with blockMesh as a single block with geometric or exponential grading that packs cells finer toward the axis (r = 0) and toward the inlet face (x = 0), with a fine-to-coarse grading ratio of approximately 3 to 5.
No boundary-layer prism layers are used.
The centerline (r = 0) uses the type axis boundary condition.
The wall (r = 0.05 m) is isothermal at T = 400 K with a noSlip velocity boundary condition.
The inlet (x = 0) supplies co-flow air with fixed-value boundary conditions: U = (10 0 0) m/s, T = 800 K, p = 101325 Pa, O2 mass fraction = 0.233, N2 mass fraction = 0.767.
The inlet also prescribes k and epsilon for the k-epsilon turbulence model, derived from a 5 percent turbulence intensity on the 10 m/s co-flow velocity.
The outlet (x = 0.2 m) uses totalPressure for p and zeroGradient for U, T, species mass fractions, k, and epsilon.
The turbulence model is standard k-epsilon with default constants.
The initial conditions throughout the domain at t = 0 are: U = (0 0 0) m/s, T = 800 K, p = 101325 Pa, O2 = 0.233, N2 = 0.767, with no fuel, no products, and k and epsilon set to zero except where the inlet BC drives them in.
The spray uses the cone injection model, positioned at the center of the inlet face (x = 0, r = 0), with a cone half-angle of 10 degrees and a liquid injection velocity of 30 m/s.
The fuel is liquid n-dodecane (nC12H26) at a droplet temperature of 300 K, with a mass flow rate of 0.002 kg/s.
The droplet size distribution is Rosin-Rammler with a mean (Sauter) diameter of 50 micrometers and the default shape parameter of 1.0.
The droplet heat and mass transfer model is RanzMarshall.
The droplet drag model is standard.
The combustion model is a two-step global finite-rate reaction mechanism for n-dodecane (fuel to intermediate, intermediate to final products), configured in constant/combustionProperties and constant/reactionSchemes using standard literature Arrhenius parameters for the usual dodecane global lumping.
The thermodynamic data for all species is sourced from Janaf tables.
The simulation runs to an end time of 0.05 s with adjustableTimeStep enabled and a maximum Courant number of 0.7.
Results are written every 0.001 s, yielding 50 output frames over the run.
